e room that used to belong to his daughter. The walls were bare now, stripped of the posters and photographs that had once covered every inch. He could still hear her laughter if he closed his eyes.

"You should sell the house," Marlene said from behind him. She had followed him up the stairs, her footsteps quiet on the old wood. "There's nothing left for you here."

"I can't," Whitmore said. "Not yet."

Detective Inspector Reyes had called that morning with news about the case. The old murder from three years ago, the one everyone in town still whispered about, had a new lead. A witness had come forward. Someone who claimed to have seen Bill Foster near the harbor the night Giselle disappeared.

Marlene frowned. "Bill Foster is dead. He died last spring."

"I know," Whitmore said. "That's what makes it strange."

Down in the kitchen, Jamie was making coffee, the smell drifting up through the house like a promise of normalcy. Jamie had been staying with Whitmore since the funeral, helping him manage the estate, though everyone in town suspected there was more to it than simple kindness. Bull, the old family dog, padded in and settled at Jamie's feet, tail thumping against the tile.

"Something's wrong," Jamie called up the stairs. "Sergeant Rhodes is here. He says it's urgent."

Whitmore closed the door to his daughter's room gently, as if she were still sleeping inside, and went down to hear what the sergeant had to say. The threat, whatever it was, would not wait for grief.

chapter_summaries.0: Giselle, a deaf painter, observes a bustling household preparing for a feast from her small room, translating the sounds and emotions she cannot hear into colors on her canvas. She paints each person—children Vin and Bran, her brother, Laurie, Sebastian, Lucius, Talia, Marlene, and Mr. Whitmore—using distinct hues that reflect their traits, while grappling with a sudden red streak that she resolves to cover with white tomorrow.
chapter_summaries.1: Sirius Wolfe reads a hand‑made anonymous letter warning of Arden Whitmore's death, confirming the writer is already dead. He reflects on his recent case catching a teenage burglar who stole a pearl necklace from 47 Marple Street, feeling guilt and fatigue. While drinking coffee and listening to his Walkman, he receives a frantic call from Pip, who reports a possible suicide of a fellow named Whitmore. Sirius decides to investigate, noting the letter is not a prank but a murder prophecy, and resolves to visit the victim’s family despite his exhaustion.
chapter_summaries.2: Detective Inspector (The Bull) storms into a room where junior detectives Jamie and Dom are discussing the death of Arden Whitmore. He learns Sergeant Rhodes is missing, threatens violence, and orders Jamie to tail a private detective while Dom must locate Rhodes and question neighbors. Tensions rise as the DI asserts authority, and several new characters are introduced, deepening the investigation into Whitmore's murder.

text_span.text: "Hello, This is private detective Sirius Wolfe."

"Sirius you won't believe what's going on 'ere. Why I was just roaming around with Penny when I saw a few constables drive past me. Almost took of Penny's head he did, that great brute, Jakob. Well, sure say we were wondering what got them up in a jiffy like that, so naturally we went out to do a bit of Espy--- espy no -- espy knowledge."

"Yes! Espionage! Me and Penny learnt it off the the book we knicked from fat Frodo as we accidently knocked him down on his way to school and helped him back up. He was thanking us so much he hardly felt Penny nip down to take out the note."

"Err ... yeah Sirius well, we were doing well you know what we came upon the Inspector's office. In right a fit of mad he was. He was flying at anyone and everyone like a rabid dog. Well he had a right reason to. See there was a suicide down here."
"A death. They say it is suicide."
"some fellow named Whitmore. Penny says he is a writer. But I don't know I haven't right hea-"
"This morning I think or last night I dunno. The police got the information right now anyway."
"Ohh. Alryt thanks for the lead. By-"
"Sirus, Sirius! You told you'd buy us a new pair of clothes the next time we inform you. I quite like a batman shirt we saw displayed on the Maris' donwtown and Penny-"
"I'll buy you all you want when I'm free Pip. Now let me be. Once I comeback, I promise."
